author: WP02
summary: The unit explains CNA's physical module layout: location as ownership, the module set, the cna_add_module factory and include roots, construction exceptions, renderer families as modules, module-owned examples, the no-loss migration and how to read a source path. At TARGET the module count (fifteen) and cna_build_flags are stale and several exceptions changed. The Development repository pages already held the inventory and edges; the reasoning, the naming traps, the partition blind spots, the example and golden ownership and a recreated ownership diagram went into a new module-architecture deep dive.

concepts.section: The Module Monorepo
concepts.text: CNA is one repository but not one library with global src/ and include/ trees; the physical module is the unit of ownership, and include spelling, link closure, optional features and which tests compile all derive from module boundaries.
tokens: its unit of ownership is the physical module

concepts.section: Location is ownership
concepts.text: A framework module has the layout modules/<name>/{CMakeLists.txt, include/, src/, tests/, examples/}, plus benchmarks/ where one exists (only diagnostics and inspector).
tokens: only diagnostics and inspector have one
concepts.note: benchmarks/ joined the owned areas after the Bible's description.

concepts.section: Location is ownership
concepts.text: The repository root deliberately has no production src/ or include/, and a configure-time guard fails if either reappears ('legacy global tree reappeared').

concepts.section: Location is ownership
concepts.text: The legacy-root guard tests CNA_SOURCE_DIR rather than CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR, because a game that adds CNA with add_subdirectory has its own root with its own src/; an earlier version failed every such consumer's configure.
concepts.note: TARGET extension.

concepts.section: Location is ownership
concepts.text: The source-partition validator recursively inventories *.cpp and Objective-C++ *.mm files and accepts a TU only under a declared framework module's or renderer family's src/, tests/, examples/ or benchmarks/; the declared lists _cna_framework_modules and _cna_renderer_modules are authoritative.
concepts.note: benchmarks/ added at TARGET.

concepts.section: Location is ownership
concepts.text: Location is stronger than tidiness: moving an implementation file changes the target that compiles it, its dependency declarations, test registration and include reachability, so the validator turns a physical move into an explicit architectural change.
tokens: The rule is stronger than tidiness

concepts.section: Location is ownership
concepts.text: The partition check sees only .cpp/.mm and path prefixes; stray headers or C files are not reported, and a TU in a subdirectory of a renderer family's src/ passes the check but is silently not compiled by the non-recursive family glob.
concepts.note: TARGET reading; recorded as WP02-i010.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: The Bible's 'fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module' is stale: TARGET declares 22 framework modules (the fifteen, c-api, and six newer modules: diagnostics, design, phone, inspector, content-pipeline and video-ffmpeg) plus modules/renderers.
concepts.note: Count corrected.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: Foundation modules: core owns CNA vocabulary and leaf infrastructure (logging, exceptions, identity enum, selection policy, the generated version header), math the XNA value and geometry types; at TARGET diagnostics joins them and platform is its own host cluster.
tokens: Leaf vocabulary with no upward edge
concepts.note: Diagnostics and a separate host cluster added.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: platform owns CNA::Platform::IPlatform and the implementations, and is the only module allowed to link a windowing or host library, always privately.
tokens: The only module allowed to link a windowing or host library
concepts.note: The Bible's 'selected implementation' omits that Headless and (POSIX) Terminal are always compiled; see the platform pages.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: runtime, graphics, input, audio and media own the game loop, the renderer-independent graphics surface, device state, the mixer and media playback; video-ffmpeg isolates every FFmpeg symbol in one optional archive.
concepts.note: video-ffmpeg added.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: content owns native, CNJ, XNB and glTF loading and storage owns Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Storage; content-pipeline keeps build-time-only code out of every game.
concepts.note: content-pipeline added.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: devices, devices-ext, graphics-ext, gamer-services and net separate faithful APIs, project extensions and networking; devices-ext must never depend on the XNA devices base, and networking is entered only with CNA_ENABLE_NET.
tokens: must never depend on the XNA devices base

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: The module aliases are narrow (CNA::Core, CNA::Math, CNA::Runtime, CNA::GraphicsCore, CNA::Input, CNA::Audio, CNA::Media, CNA::Content, CNA::Storage, CNA::Devices, CNA::DevicesExt, CNA::GraphicsExt), with CNA::GamerServices and CNA::Net only when networking is enabled.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: The appendix maps every module to its pinned role without inferring a dependency graph from the inventory.
concepts.note: Cross-reference between parts of the source text; the TARGET module map and its edges are on the Development repository pages.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: With CNA_BUILD_C_API=ON, modules/c-api defines the shared cna_c_api / CNA::CApi target that wraps the canonical C++ modules and exports C17 headers; it is an adapter, not another framework implementation.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: The claim that at TARGET the C API library builds and installs with the canonical module graph is not established: no workflow builds it.

concepts.section: Fifteen framework modules and one optional ABI module
concepts.text: The C API release gate reports not ready; the old renderer-identity compile blocker is gone from the source.
concepts.note: The Bible attributes the red gate to coverage-inventory reasons; a TARGET comment attributes it to open packaging decisions. Kept to the verdict only.

concepts.section: The module factory and one public include root
concepts.text: cna_add_module(target alias ...) creates a STATIC cna_<name> library with alias CNA::<Alias>, links the public build configuration and publishes the module's own include/; the shared surface is cna_build_config (CNA::BuildConfig), not the Bible's cna_build_flags.
concepts.note: Target renamed.

concepts.section: The module factory and one public include root
concepts.text: Every module exports exactly its own include/ directory; no module exports its src/.
tokens: Every module exports exactly its own include/

concepts.section: The module factory and one public include root
concepts.text: A header needed across modules lives under a public include root, usually include/CNA/Internal/ for engine seams; 'Internal' is a naming and review convention, not a visibility barrier.

concepts.section: The module factory and one public include root
concepts.text: The Bible names renderer-local shader headers as the only src/ exception; at TARGET module-private headers under src/ are common (platform has over a hundred) and there are exactly two cross-module src/ reaches: renderers include modules/platform/src and the test build includes modules/audio/src.
concepts.note: The cna_add_module comment repeating the old rule is stale.

concepts.section: The module factory and one public include root
concepts.text: Consumer include spelling is unchanged because the module root is removed by the include path: #include <Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Game.hpp>, <Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/Texture2D.hpp>, <CNA/GraphicsRendererType.hpp>.

concepts.section: The module factory and one public include root
concepts.text: Code must not embed repository-relative prefixes such as modules/runtime/include/; the physical path identifies the owner for reviewers and is not the public spelling.
tokens: it is not the public spelling

concepts.section: Two deliberate construction exceptions
concepts.text: gamer-services and net hand-build CNA_GamerServices and CNA_Net with add_library instead of cna_add_module; at TARGET video-ffmpeg and c-api are hand-built too, and 18 of the 22 framework modules use the factory.
concepts.note: Two more exceptions at TARGET.

concepts.section: Two deliberate construction exceptions
concepts.text: Tooling that derives concrete target names from directory names is wrong for several modules (graphics is cna_graphics_core, content-pipeline's alias is CNA::ContentPipelineBuild, gamer-services is CNA_GamerServices); use aliases or read the module's CMake file.

concepts.section: Two deliberate construction exceptions
concepts.text: cna_core_headers (CNA::CoreHeaders) exposes core's leaf declarations (CNAEXT marker, PlayerIndex, path containment) without linking cna_core; math and storage use it, and at TARGET platform, phone and inspector too, keeping link closures exact.

target.evidence: modules/core/CMakeLists.txt; math, storage, platform, phone, inspector CMakeLists.txt

concepts.note: Three more users at TARGET.

concepts.section: Two deliberate construction exceptions
concepts.text: The generated CNA/Version.hpp is written into <CNA build dir>/generated/include by cmake/Version.cmake (using CNA_BINARY_DIR for subproject builds) and rides the core include roots.
concepts.note: TARGET extension.

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: modules/renderers declares 21 implementation families plus shared infrastructure (common/d3d, common/mojoshader).

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: Only the selected family is normally entered; in a multi-renderer build each distinct family is entered once, and each builds cna_renderer_<family>; the name is derived from the family's own directory rather than a global variable.
tokens: enters one directory per distinct selected family

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: One family can carry several identities: EasyGL owns five GL profiles, which is why the registry has 25 identities and the tree 21 families.
tokens: Only the EasyGL family carries more than one public identity

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: The common setup gives each family its include root, the common build interface, the sharp-runtime closure and reverse links to graphics, core and math; at TARGET the family's own identity macro is private to its target and the platform source root is added privately.
concepts.note: Private identity macro and platform/src root added.

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: The renderer source glob is deliberately non-recursive, so a nested translation unit does not join the target merely because it exists on disk.

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: Platform-specific renderer header targets stay defined when another renderer is selected because their policy suites compile into the shared tests; at TARGET this applies only to metal.
concepts.note: A second family with the same arrangement was retired; names withheld by policy.

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: common/d3d is entered only for Direct3D 11 and 12 (when the default identity is one of them); DIRECTX9 has an independent implementation.
tokens: DIRECTX9 has its own independent implementation
concepts.note: Default-identity condition made explicit; a retired family mentioned in the Bible is omitted by policy.

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: GDI reuses eight software-renderer 2D translation units and a software header target; physical ownership stays with software.

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: These are declared source relationships, not permission for arbitrary cross-family includes; at TARGET Vulkan examples also compile EasyGL example sources verbatim to share golden images.
tokens: Cross-family source sharing is always declared and never implicit

concepts.section: Renderer families are physical modules too
concepts.text: The generated registry maps the compiled identity set to the physical family targets and latches one active family at run time.
tokens: latches one family at run time

concepts.section: Examples moved to their owners
concepts.text: Framework examples live beside the subsystem they demonstrate, renderer examples beside their family and CNAEXT examples under graphics-ext.

concepts.section: Examples moved to their owners
concepts.text: The graphics module owns shared renderer-agnostic fixtures (the 2D demo, pixel-test helpers) and family example files reach them through CNA_GRAPHICS_EXAMPLES_DIR.

concepts.section: Examples moved to their owners
concepts.text: The repository-level examples/ keeps examples/golden, 17 PNGs captured from EasyGL and also used by Vulkan tests, loaded through repository-root-relative paths (tests run with the repository root as working directory), plus one loose demo source; the goldens are CNA captures, not an XNA oracle.
tokens: 17 reference PNGs captured from the EasyGL renderer
concepts.note: The Bible calls it the cross-renderer image-oracle corpus with one owner-less purpose.

concepts.section: Examples moved to their owners
concepts.text: Executables are still emitted at the build root for compatibility (module example files set CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY), so output location is not evidence of ownership.

concepts.section: The migration was checked as a no-loss transformation
concepts.text: The physical-module campaign moved 1,776 files in seven pure-rename commits before rewriting the build.
concepts.note: Campaign history from August 2026; the page keeps the reconciliation figures that the repository still records and does not re-count commits.

concepts.section: The migration was checked as a no-loss transformation
concepts.text: Its reconciliation classified 1,357 production files: 1,287 byte-identical moves, 70 with only include-path directives changed, none lost; CTest names in HEADLESS and OPENGLES configurations had no removals or renames.
concepts.note: The record carries its own historical banner.

concepts.section: The migration was checked as a no-loss transformation
concepts.text: Later changes are easy to conflate with the move: module-local example registration removed the central manifests and renderer terminology replaced backend-named files, so older paths may be historically real but absent now.

target.evidence: git history; absence of cmake/CnaLibrary.cmake, BackendLibraries.cmake, Examples.cmake at TARGET

concepts.section: The migration was checked as a no-loss transformation
concepts.text: Stale pre-campaign paths survive in the Metal workflow's push filter, which lists three missing files and omits the Metal family's own CMake files, so registration-only changes do not trigger it on push.
concepts.note: TARGET finding; WP02-i004.

concepts.section: How to read a source path in this book
concepts.text: A path such as modules/content/src/Xna/ContentManager.cpp carries three claims (the owner, private implementation, public include root) and does not prove which umbrella links it, which features compiled it or which runtime path called it.

concepts.section: How to read a source path in this book
concepts.text: An architecture claim needs four artifacts read together: the file's module, that module's CMakeLists.txt, the root composition and partition rules, and a link or execution artifact of the selected configuration.
